entries.question: How does Duplicate Node & Cell Resolution decide which record is correct?
entries.answer: It forms duplicate groups on the key (Node ID or Cell Name), scores each member on evidence (presence in the latest dump, NMS ownership, site consistency, cell-to-node mapping and naming rules) and classifies each group as Correct ID/Cell Identified, Having Issue, Removed (stale member) or Manual Validation Required. Tiles show Total Nodes, Dup Node IDs, Dup Cells and Correct Records. Unresolvable groups are routed to the owning team.

entries.question: What is the Baseline Parameter Audit?
entries.answer: It selects the approved baseline for each cell by technology, band and vendor (from the Reporting and Attribute Details workbook), compares configured values such as Bandwidth DL/UL and EARFCN DL/UL with the baseline, counts deviations per parameter and lists the deviating cells for a parameter-correction work order.

entries.question: How does the Cell-to-RU Mapping Suggestion work?
alternate_questions: Suggest RRU model for unmapped cells
entries.answer: It audits cells for a mapped radio unit (Hardware Mapped vs Missing HW). For cells without hardware, it learns RRU models used by comparable cells (same node, band, vendor) across reports ('model learning: multi-report frequency'), suggests the most frequent model with a High or Low confidence class and ranks the suggested RRU types. The dashboard shows Mapping Completeness (Hardware Mapped, AI Auto-Suggested High/Low Confidence, Unmapped Missing HW).

entries.question: What does 5G Upgrade Readiness show?
alternate_questions: Which sites can be upgraded to 5G?
entries.answer: It classifies every site (5G Active, 5G Not Available, Ghost Node, Site No Longer Present, Unknown Hardware), checks installed hardware of target sites against 5G compatibility, and classifies the upgrade path: Ready to Upgrade to 5G, HW Available/Compatible (SW Upgrade), HW Not Available/Compatible (HW Swap), Partial Upgrade Possible or Unknown Hardware. Useful for 5G rollout planning.

entries.question: How does GPS Suggestion impute missing coordinates?
entries.answer: For sites with missing or invalid GPS (GPS Accuracy Audit), NETIQ searches other source reports in order (RAN Site Report, 2G/4G/5G Cell Reports, Transmission Site Report, Planned vs Configured Link Report), takes valid coordinates for the same site and records the source report. Sites with no source are 'GPS Not Identified'. Summaries cover GPS Suggested %, source-wise counts, technology-wise status and circle-wise success rate.

entries.question: How are AI suggestions governed?
entries.answer: Discovered and inferred values are stored and shown separately; every suggestion carries a confidence (score or High/Low class) and its evidence; suggestions are reviewed in the dashboard drill-down and only accepted values are written back with source tagging; results the model cannot resolve go to manual validation by the owning team; and counts and models are validated against field data before AI Intelligence leaves BETA.

entries.question: What do Site, Node and Cell Inference reports contain?
entries.answer: Site Inference predicts the correct Site ID for each record with a remark (for example 'Site ID correct - no issue') and proposes a Site ID where the dump leaves it unidentified. Node and Cell Inference complete node and cell relationships and attributes with a confidence and remark. Typical columns: Circle, predicted/inferred identity, Node/Cell Name, Remark, Vendor, EMS IP.

entries.question: What is the Network Truth Repository?
alternate_questions: What is the single source of truth?
What reports are in the repository?
entries.answer: The normalised, audited single-source-of-truth inventory for nodes, cells, hardware, ports, links and IP across every domain, organised as RAN, TXN (Transport), FTTH and Wireline repositories. Each record carries source, site source and insert/update provenance. All grids share the common toolbar (columns, filters, export, advanced query).

entries.question: Which reports are in the RAN Repository?
alternate_questions: Where do I find eNodeB data?
entries.answer: Node reports (All Nodes, BTS 2G, eNodeB 4G, gNodeB 5G, SRAN, Ghost Nodes), Cell reports (2G, 4G, 5G), Hardware Report, Cabinet Report, IP Data Report and Core / Network IP Report. Node reports show Circle, Node ID, Node Name, Site ID, Site Source, Latitude, Longitude and Location Source.

entries.question: Which reports are in the TXN, FTTH and Wireline repositories?
entries.answer: TXN: Site, Node, Hardware, Port, MW Link, UBR Link, IP, VLAN and Planned vs Configured Link reports. FTTH: Node Inventory, Hardware, Link and Port reports. Wireline: Node Inventory, Hardware, Port, Logical Inventory, VLAN Report and Link Inventory. The Wireline logical inventory is the largest dataset (millions of rows) and is served with server-side pagination.

entries.question: What key fields are in the RAN Node and 4G Cell reports?
alternate_questions: What fields are in the cell report?
entries.answer: Node Report: Node_ID (for example MRBTS-901305), Node_Name, Vendor, Technology (highest present), Latitude, Longitude, Cabinet_Model, Product_Code, Primary_IP and more. 4G Cell Report: Node ID/Name, Site ID, Site ID Source, EnodeB ID/Name, MCC, MNC, Cell Name, Cell ID, TAC, EARFCN UL/DL, Bandwidth UL/DL, plus CGI, admin status and duplex mode. 5G and 2G schemas are defined analogously in the Solution Document section 15.

entries.question: What is the Decommission Ledger?
alternate_questions: How do I verify a site tear-down?
What is the Deleted Reports view?
entries.answer: A complete, auditable log of retired, deleted and decommissioned assets across RAN (NMS, Site, Node, Cell, Hardware inventory) and Transport (NMS, Site, Node, Hardware). Entities that disappear from a dump (the Deleted count on dashboards) land here. A date-range control (All Time or Days) answers questions such as 'what was decommissioned this week?' and supports tear-down reconciliation for change tickets.

entries.question: The Decommission Ledger shows 'No data found'. What should I do?
entries.answer: Widen the date range (for example All Time) or clear the column filters. The combination of filters may be too narrow for the chosen period or circle.

entries.question: What is the Planned vs Configured Link Report?
entries.answer: A transport report comparing the planned link design (MIDS plan) with what is discovered in the network. It lists planned HOP sites, NMS status (Matched / Unmatched), frequency, channel spacing, modulation and HOP type. It underpins Deployment Compliance, the Missing Txn Links insight and the AI Frequency Deviation dashboard, and the stitching AI audit uses it as supporting evidence.

entries.question: What does the MW Link Report contain?
entries.answer: Link identity and the two sites and NEs (Link ID, Site 1/Site 2, NE ID 1/2), TX/RX frequency channels, cabinet/shelf/slot/index/port details of each end and D-XPIC TX/RX frequency, along with capacity, modulation, link configuration (for example 1+0, 1+1, XPIC) and status. It is a primary input for hop-chain tracing in stitching.

entries.question: What is the recommended daily operational routine?
alternate_questions: What should I check every morning?
entries.answer: Confirm each domain's latest collection cycle completed (scheduler record / last-refreshed); review discovery counts and the NMS health gauge for unexpected drops; work new high-severity audit findings and coordinate source corrections; confirm corrected findings clear next cycle and track the stitch-percentage trend; review the reject summary and re-ingest corrected files where needed.

entries.question: How is platform health monitored?
alternate_questions: How do I know NETIQ is healthy?
entries.answer: Through the NMS health gauge and the 'All systems operational' status tile (with last-updated time), the scheduler-completion record per domain, records loaded/rejected per cycle, audit-finding volume by severity and Stitch %. These are complemented by infrastructure-level monitoring of the tiers.

entries.question: What is the support model and who handles which tier?
alternate_questions: Who do I contact for support?
entries.answer: L1: first-line triage of anomalies and user queries (NOC/Operations). L2: data-quality investigation and source-correction coordination (Operations/Audit/Admin). L3: platform, rule and configuration issues (Avendum support / Super Admin). Response and resolution SLAs per severity and tier are to be agreed with the customer and recorded; they are not fixed in the documents.

entries.question: What are the support contact details?
entries.answer: The user manual leaves contact fields (help channels and escalation contacts) as placeholders to be completed per organisation. In the meantime, contact your NETIQ administrator, who can escalate to the Avendum support team. For problems not covered by the manual, the same route applies.

entries.question: What is the backup, RPO, RTO and disaster recovery approach?
alternate_questions: What is the RPO and RTO?
How do we recover from failure?
entries.answer: Regular backup of inventory, audit results and configuration (sources, rules, schedules, users/roles). To recover, restore the latest backup to a standby environment and re-run collection; because ingestion is idempotent, this re-establishes the live state without duplication. Concrete backup frequency, RPO/RTO targets and DR topology are to be agreed with the customer and are not fixed in the document.

entries.question: Is NETIQ highly available?
entries.answer: The design targets high availability for the web/application tier (minimum 99.5% console uptime target), while the processing tier runs on the collection schedule and tolerates a missed cycle without data loss. Exact HA topology (co-located or separated tiers) depends on the deployment.

entries.question: What are the main risks and their mitigations?
entries.answer: Incomplete/delayed source exports (monitor scheduler, alert on missing cycles, agree source SLAs); poor source data quality (continuous audits, fix-at-source, trend tracking); inconsistent identifiers across sources (normalisation, duplicate and mapping audits, AI inference); volume growth (capacity planning, server-side pagination, scale infrastructure); and RBAC misconfiguration (periodic access reviews, least privilege).

entries.question: What training is available for NETIQ?
alternate_questions: How do we train our team?
entries.answer: Role-based training anchored on the User Manual: end users/read-only (navigation, dashboards, exports), operations/NOC (monitoring, triage, validation, escalation), audit (running and interpreting audits, exception handling) and administrators (users/roles, scheduler, rules, configuration). Knowledge transfer covers architecture, data flows, rule configuration and runbooks. New users can also launch the in-app Platform Tour.

entries.question: How does cutover work, and is there a risk to existing systems?
entries.answer: Because NETIQ is read-and-reconcile and consumes source exports, cutover is low-risk: collection is enabled per domain, the first cycles establish the baseline, and audits and stitching improve as source data is corrected. No destructive migration of source systems is required.

entries.question: What are the acceptance criteria for NETIQ?
entries.answer: Parser accuracy of 99% or more per vendor/technology; audit detection rate of 100% for seeded High-severity issues and 98% or more for seeded Medium severity; and all mandatory columns populated in the Node/Cell/HW report schemas. Acceptance is validated through the defined test cases and UAT on production-like data against functional coverage, reporting accuracy and non-functional targets.

entries.question: What test cases are defined for NETIQ?
entries.answer: PAN-01 (PAN India totals equal the sum of Circle totals, 100% match); circle-level aggregation and vendor/technology splits; SITE-01 to SITE-05 (site count, no orphan sites, cells per site, GPS completeness, Site ID consistency between node and cell); node and cell availability; VAL-06 to VAL-11 duplicate checks (node name/ID, cell name/ID, IP, VLAN); VAL-12/13 missing class and attribute; VAL-22/23 cabinet and board completeness; and VAL-26/27 GPS completeness and range.

entries.question: Who signs off and what is the UAT approach?
entries.answer: UAT validates against production-like data in the UAT environment: functional coverage (section 12), reporting and audit accuracy (sections 15-18) and non-functional targets (sections 21-22). Sign-off roles are Solution Architect, Operations/NOC Lead, Delivery Manager and Customer SPOC, who accepts for production use.

entries.question: A dashboard or the Service Path Explorer does not render correctly. What should I check?
entries.answer: Use a supported, current browser (Chrome, Edge or Firefox; not Internet Explorer); hard-refresh or clear the cache; reset browser zoom to 100% and use at least 1366x768 (1920x1080 recommended); disable ad-blockers or script-blocking extensions, or test in a private/incognito window; and allow pop-ups and downloads for the NETIQ site.

entries.question: I see 'No data for the selected filters'. What does it mean?
entries.answer: The filter combination returns nothing, often because the date range, circle or technology is too narrow. Widen or clear the filters (use Reset All) and try again.

entries.question: Export failed or the file did not download. What should I do?
entries.answer: Retry the export. If it recurs, check that the browser is not blocking pop-ups or downloads for the NETIQ site (see browser issues) and that the filtered result set is not excessively large. If it persists, note the exact message and screen and pass it to support.

entries.question: I get 'Unable to load' or 'something went wrong'. What now?
entries.answer: It is usually a transient loading problem. Refresh the page; if it continues, clear the browser cache or sign out and back in. If it still persists, report the exact wording and the screen to support.

entries.question: My session expired. What should I do?
entries.answer: Sessions expire after a period of inactivity for security and return you to the login screen. Sign in again. The exact timeout is set by deployment policy.

entries.question: The data in NETIQ differs from my NMS. Why?
alternate_questions: Counts do not match my NMS
entries.answer: NETIQ reflects the last collected CM dump, so data freshness is bounded by the collection cadence. Differences can also be genuine: NETIQ reconciles multiple sources and flags ghost elements, duplicates, naming and mapping inconsistencies that the individual NMS may not show. Check the last-updated indicator, the NMS Updated/Non-Updated status for that NMS and the relevant audit report; correct at source and confirm after the next cycle.

entries.question: Why does a finding still appear after the data was fixed?
alternate_questions: I fixed the issue but it still shows
entries.answer: The corrected CM dump has not been ingested yet. Findings clear automatically on the next cycle after the corrected data is ingested. Confirm the NMS dump was refreshed and check the reject summary in case the corrected rows were rejected.

entries.question: Why is a site missing from the Service Path Explorer map or shown with wrong location?
entries.answer: Site coordinates come from the Site Report, falling back to the 'Default LATITUDE_LONGITUDE' sheet (never for Core sites). Missing or invalid GPS also blocks geo-based searches. Check the GPS Accuracy Audit and GPS Suggestion for that site and correct the source coordinates.

entries.question: What does CM dump mean?
alternate_questions: What is a configuration management dump?
entries.answer: Configuration Management export: the raw configuration data collected from each NMS/EMS each cycle, which NETIQ parses and normalises.

entries.question: What is an Access POP (L2) and an AGW (L3 POP)?
entries.answer: L2 (Access POP) is the first Wireline node on a RAN service path that carries the RAN VLAN but not the RAN Gateway IP. AGW (Aggregation Gateway, L3 POP) is the Wireline node whose WAN IP equals the RAN Gateway IP.

entries.question: What do SRAN, BTS, eNodeB, gNodeB, RU and RRU mean?
entries.answer: BTS/eNodeB/gNodeB are 2G/4G/5G base stations; SRAN is Single RAN, a combined multi-technology radio node; RU/RRU is the (Remote) Radio Unit serving cells.

entries.question: What do CGI, TAC, LAC, EARFCN and FDD/TDD mean?
entries.answer: CGI is Cell Global Identity (CGI = MCC-MNC-TAC/LAC-CI); TAC/LAC are Tracking/Location Area Codes; EARFCN is the carrier frequency channel number of an LTE cell; FDD/TDD are Frequency/Time Division Duplexing.

entries.question: What do MW, UBR, FTTH and Wireline refer to in NETIQ?
entries.answer: MW is Microwave transport links; UBR is Ultra Broadband Radio links; FTTH is fibre-access (ONT/OLT) nodes and links; Wireline is the fixed-line backhaul/aggregation domain with nodes, ports, logical inventory, VLANs and links.

entries.question: What is BOQ in the Service Path Explorer?
entries.answer: Bill of Quantity: a consolidated count of discovered assets shown as KPI cards (Total Sites, Fully Stitched, Partial, Unresolved, Suggested and Stitch %).

entries.question: What do RBAC, KPI, SLA, RPO and RTO mean in the documents?
entries.answer: RBAC: Role-Based Access Control; KPI: Key Performance Indicator; SLA: Service Level Agreement; RPO/RTO: Recovery Point / Recovery Time Objective.

entries.question: What is VLAN Match % and Deployment Compliance?
entries.answer: VLAN Match % = common VLANs between a port VLAN trunk and the RAN VLAN group, divided by the RAN VLAN group size, x 100. Deployment Compliance = planned links deployed and matched divided by total planned links x 100.
